evaluation.decides: Approving fixes what a customer can do in the first release: reserve a loaf for the next morning until 18:00 and pick it up in a slot. The baker's own view (US1.2) is named but not written yet.

lookFirst.text: US1.2, the baker's list of tomorrow's orders, has no description and no acceptance criteria.
lookFirst.why: The baker is the one who bakes from it; without criteria nobody can say when it is done, and the next stages will guess.

lookFirst.text: The 18:00 cut-off in AC1.1.2 is new here: the requirements never name a closing time.
lookFirst.why: A cut-off decides how much the bakery can plan; it should be the owner's call, not the stories'.

solid.text: The customer's story is one visible behaviour with Given/When/Then criteria a tester can follow.

risks.text: Slots hold at most eight orders (FR2.2), but no criterion says what a customer sees when a slot is full.

gaps.text: FR2.1's 15-minute slots between 07:00 and 10:00 are not in any criterion yet.

review-2.note: Nothing in US1.2 can be tested.

review-3.note: A full slot is not covered.

earlier-requirements.note: FR2.1 and FR2.2 are reflected, the cut-off is an addition (look first).

US1.summary: Everything a customer does to reserve bread for the next morning.
US1.label: medium

US1.1.summary: A customer reserves a loaf for tomorrow until 18:00 and gets a confirmation; after 18:00 ordering is closed.
US1.1.label: high

US1.2.summary: The baker sees tomorrow's orders; the story is named but has no text or criteria yet.
US1.2.label: high
